review_comments.body: ** Major** · **Stability & Availability** · **Quick win** **Normalize the string-keyed event type too.** A payload such as `{"event_type" => "action", "ts" => timestamp}` retains `"event_type"` and adds `:event_type`. The sanitizer retains both keys, so JSON 3.1.0 raises `JSON::GeneratorError` during upload. This can block the batch, despite the timestamp fix. Remove the string key before assigning `:event_type`, and add a round-trip test for a fully string-keyed payload. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/honeybadger-io/honeybadger-ruby/ee1e703a32c69005b77eec7a791d4132a352ce6a/lib/honeybadger/util/sanitizer.rb))

comments.body:
Walkthrough

Event initialization now uses a string-keyed `"ts"` value if `:ts` is absent, before generating a timestamp. JSON serialization removes the string-keyed entry and sets `:ts` to the event timestamp. Added specs cover both constructor forms and verify that `:ts` takes precedence when both keys are present. **Suggested reviewers:** `stympy`
**Change:** Bug fix
Merge Risk: Low · up to ee1e7

The timestamp fix works for string-keyed payloads. Events whose event type is also supplied under a string key can still produce duplicate JSON keys and fail upload on JSON 3.1.0. That behavior predates this change, but it is closely related and cheap to fix, so consider addressing it before or soon after merge.
